name: Cinder Skipper
description: A palm-sized lizard grazes on charcoal after forest fires, leaving warm footprints that fade in seconds.
attacks: Spark kick: Dexterity + Athletics to hit; 1 bashing damage die.
notes: Once per scene, it scatters embers in a one-meter patch. Crossing that patch costs one extra meter of movement for two turns. Wet ground prevents this trick.
appearance: Tiny rust-red lizard with six legs, broad ribbed ear fins and a blunt charcoal snout, perched on cooled volcanic stone in a burned forest; faint sparks trail its feet.
ecology: Cinder Skippers colonize recently burned woodland, scraping charcoal and the fungi beneath it from fallen branches. They lay eggs in ash-filled hollows that retain warmth overnight; adults disperse when fresh growth shades the ground. Birds take most hatchlings. Small black pellets and six-pointed tracks identify a feeding site. Their grazing opens cracks in charred bark where seedlings can root.

name: Rainspool Grazer
description: This barrel-shaped marsh herbivore winds fallen reeds around its back, carrying an accidental floating garden.
attacks: Shoulder shove: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing.
notes: After spending a turn drinking, it can spray stored water over a two-meter patch. This extinguishes ordinary candles and reveals footprints in loose dust, but causes no damage.
appearance: Low barrel-shaped teal amphibian with four paddle feet and a spiral of woven reeds on its back, standing in a shallow marsh under drizzle.
ecology: Rainspool Grazers browse submerged shoots in shallow freshwater marshes. Algae and snails colonize the reeds on their backs, providing food for small wading birds that follow the herd. Pairs build floating reed nurseries and guard soft-skinned young until their paddle feet strengthen. In drought they crowd the remaining pools, stripping vegetation and leaving broad muddy channels between them.

name: Bellreed Darter
description: A silver marsh insect rings hollow reeds with its rigid antennae to announce approaching rain.
attacks: Needle jab: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 bashing damage die.
notes: Its alarm carries 100 meters in still air. A listener who spends a turn attending to the rhythm gains one die on the next roll to locate moving water during the scene.
appearance: A single delicate silver insect with long tuning-fork antennae and clear paddle-shaped wings, balanced on the rim of a hollow reed above a pond.
ecology: Bellreed Darters breed in hollow reeds above quiet ponds. Their aquatic larvae eat mosquito larvae, while adults take pollen and drink condensation. Males and females identify each other by the pitch of their antenna taps. Reed cutting destroys whole breeding colonies. A pond that has fallen silent may have been drained, poisoned or occupied by something that has driven its insects away.

name: Chalkback Burrower
description: A squat digger feeds on soft mineral seams and coughs up chalk pellets that map its tunnel network.
attacks: Blunt tusks: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing.
notes: A turn of frantic digging raises a one-meter dust cloud lasting two turns. Sight-based searches through it lose two dice; sound and scent are unaffected.
appearance: Squat six-footed cream-colored burrowing animal with blunt shovel tusks and layered chalk plates across its back, beside pale limestone tunnels.
ecology: Chalkback Burrowers follow damp limestone seams, eating mineral crusts and the microbes growing beneath them. Family groups share branching tunnels, with nursery chambers above the flood line. Young animals inherit a section of tunnel when the group divides. Their chalk pellets mark feeding routes and attract salt-seeking insects; their abandoned chambers shelter bats, but fresh excavation can undermine old foundations.

name: Mossveil Glider
description: A canopy scavenger folds its fringed flight membrane over itself to resemble a hanging clump of moss.
attacks: Hooked feet: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 lethal damage die.
notes: It can glide twenty meters from a five-meter perch but cannot gain height. While hanging motionless in foliage, it gains two dice to Stealth; movement ends the bonus.
appearance: Small emerald mammal with a fringed mosslike gliding membrane stretched between four limbs, hanging beneath a wet branch in a shadowy canopy.
ecology: Mossveil Gliders live in humid forest canopies, feeding on beetle grubs, fallen fruit and eggs left unattended. A pair raises its young in a bark pocket lined with shed membrane fringe. They need continuous trees to travel safely and rarely cross open ground. Owls find them when they unfold to glide. Their droppings spread fruit seeds between isolated branches and tree hollows.

name: Pebblejaw Forager
description: This short-legged seed eater stores polished stones in cheek pouches and trades them for unfamiliar food.
attacks: Stone spit: Dexterity + Athletics; 2 bashing damage dice within five meters.
notes: It carries three stones and spends a turn retrieving each replacement. A new flavor of food distracts it for one turn unless it has already tasted that food this scene.
appearance: Round ochre seed-eating animal with short legs, oversized stone-filled cheek pouches and two tiny ivory incisors, arranging shiny pebbles on a woodland path.
ecology: Pebblejaw Foragers occupy the edges of mixed woodland, where seeds, hard nuts and stream-polished stones are plentiful. Several related adults share a burrow but keep separate stone piles. Young learn which foods are safe by exchanging morsels with adults. Forgotten seed caches sprout around their dens. Campsites offering unfamiliar food can draw the whole colony out of cover and attract its predators.

name: Bristlefin Wader
description: A shoreline hunter spreads stiff dorsal bristles to hold its place in fast currents.
attacks: Fin rake: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength lethal.
notes: If it remains still for a turn in running water, dislodging it requires three successes on Strength + Athletics. The anchor ends as soon as it attacks or moves.
appearance: Long green aquatic animal on four stiltlike legs with a high comb of stiff copper bristles along its spine, braced in a rushing stream.
ecology: Bristlefin Waders stake out fast, shallow streams and eat mussels, insect larvae and small fish. They wedge eggs into gravel pockets sheltered behind stones; adults defend these sites from dredging and disturbance. Their dorsal bristles wear down during flood season and regrow in calmer months. Rows of opened shells mark a territory. Removing a wader often allows burrowing prey to loosen the stream bank.

name: Coppercrest Runner
description: A flightless scavenger nests near rail yards, polishing its broad crest against discarded wire.
attacks: Crest butt: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength + 1 bashing.
notes: Metallic clattering draws its attention before voices do. Offering a loose bolt lets a handler attempt Manipulation + Animal Kinship at difficulty 6 to redirect it for one turn.
appearance: Lean flightless rust-feathered bird with long springy legs and a broad burnished copper head crest, standing among railway ballast and discarded wire.
ecology: Coppercrest Runners thrive around warm rail ballast, feeding on spilled grain, weeds and insects beneath discarded metal. Pairs decorate ground nests with wire and bolts; a bright, crowded nest attracts mates but is easy for scavengers to find. Chicks follow the sound of their parents tapping a crest. Their collecting sometimes strips small fittings from unattended equipment, bringing them into conflict with maintenance crews.

name: Hushpelt Tracker
description: A long-bodied dusk hunter follows the warmth left by resting animals rather than their scent.
attacks: Clamping jaws: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength lethal.
notes: It gains two dice to follow a trail less than ten minutes old on dry ground. Rain or a crossing through water ends this bonus. A heated blanket can create a false resting place.
appearance: Long low indigo-furred hunter with six slender legs, a broad sensitive nose and velvet ears folded flat, sniffing a warm hollow in twilight grass.
ecology: Hushpelt Trackers hunt alone at dusk along sheltered game trails. They eat small burrowing animals and return to recently vacated nests while the bedding is still warm. Females raise litters beneath windthrown roots, bringing the young prey that has just stopped moving. Heavy rain forces them to hunt by ordinary sight and hearing. Repeatedly warmed bedding can draw one back to an otherwise empty campsite.

name: Saltglass Crawler
description: A tidal grazer grows transparent salt scales that cloud over as fresh water approaches.
attacks: Shell edge: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 lethal damage die; Athletics defaults to zero.
notes: Fresh water dissolves one point of its Armor for the scene after a full turn of contact. A shed scale is a useful humidity indicator but has no protective value.
appearance: Hand-sized translucent snail-like shoreline animal with angular salt-crystal plates and four soft feelers, creeping over black tidal rocks.
ecology: Saltglass Crawlers graze microbial films on exposed tidal rocks. They deposit translucent egg clusters inside salt-lined cracks, and hatchlings begin growing armor after their first drying tide. Storm runoff drives adults toward the open sea. Shorebirds eat individuals whose scales have softened. Shed plates accumulate above the high-water mark and support tiny salt-tolerant lichens long after the crawler has moved on.

name: Thornbasket Nestling
description: A juvenile climber weaves thorn stems into a traveling nest and drags it from shrub to shrub.
attacks: Thorn nudge: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 bashing damage die.
notes: When frightened it retreats into its basket, gaining one Armor while stationary. A turn spent offering ripe fruit coaxes it back out; the basket bonus then ends.
appearance: Tiny tawny climbing mammal with huge black eyes and a curling tail, peeking from a spherical nest woven of green thorn stems on a shrub.
ecology: Thornbasket Nestlings are the juvenile stage of a solitary shrub climber. They eat berries and soft shoots, adding fresh thorn stems to their traveling nests as they grow. At maturity they anchor the basket high in a thorn tree, use it as a breeding den and forage without carrying it. Empty baskets shelter insects and small birds. Clearing hedgerows removes both their food and their nurseries.

name: Dewcup Drifter
description: This floating seed-eater traps morning dew in a cup-shaped sail and rides slow currents of warm air.
attacks: No damaging attack; an evasive drift uses Dexterity + Athletics.
notes: Its sail holds one mouthful of water. A heavy spray grounds it for the scene, while shelter and one turn of drying restore its ability to float a meter above the ground.
appearance: A single small pale-gold airborne animal with a cup-shaped leaf sail, dangling soft tendrils and a bead of dew in its sail, floating in a misty meadow.
ecology: Dewcup Drifters gather over meadows at sunrise, catching airborne seeds in the damp lining of their sails. Mature animals release threadlike eggs onto tall grass; the young float only after their first sail dries. Swallows pick them from rising air, while prolonged rain leaves them exposed to ground feeders. Their droppings sow grasses on ledges and roofs that ordinary seed-eating animals seldom reach.

name: Sootpatch Scavenger
description: A broad-tailed alley omnivore rubs soot into its coat and leaves misleading smudges around its food caches.
attacks: Tail slap: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing; Athletics defaults to zero.
notes: It remembers three hidden caches. Following its outward tracks leads to a decoy unless a searcher gets two successes on Perception + Investigation at difficulty 6.
appearance: A stocky slate-gray alley animal with a broad flat tail and soot-black patches around amber eyes, sitting beside brickwork with dark paw smudges.
ecology: Sootpatch Scavengers eat kitchen scraps, beetles and rooftop fruit, sleeping in disused flues that retain warmth. Mothers divide food among several caches before bringing young out of the nest. Rival scavengers follow soot trails and frequently dig up the decoys. A sudden disappearance of chimney smudges often means a flue has been relit. Their real stores draw insects into walls and can spread seeds through a neighborhood.

name: Rootknuckle Browser
description: A slow forest browser levers buried roots from the earth with a pair of knuckled feeding limbs.
attacks: Root lever: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength + 1 bashing.
notes: After two uninterrupted turns, it can uproot a small sapling or break a wooden fence panel. Loud repeated tapping makes it stop feeding for one turn, once per scene.
appearance: Heavy moss-brown herbivore with four walking legs and two thick jointed digging arms, a blunt beak and ridged shoulders, pulling roots beside a fallen tree.
ecology: Rootknuckle Browsers move slowly through mature woodland, eating starchy roots and bark softened by rot. Adults usually travel alone, meeting at exposed mineral beds to breed. A calf follows its parent through a full growing season before establishing its own feeding circuit. Their digging aerates compacted soil and creates pools, but several browsers confined to a small wood can uproot nearly every young tree.

name: Kiln Porter
description: A walking stack of fired clay rings carries hot objects for an absent workshop owner.
attacks: Ceramic fist: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing; Brawl defaults to zero.
notes: It can handle ordinary hot cookware without injury. A direct application of cold water makes its joints seize for one turn; repeated splashing has no further effect that scene.
appearance: A stout walking automaton made from stacked terracotta kiln rings, thick ceramic arms and a glowing furnace slit, carrying an empty iron tray in a pottery workshop.
ecology: Kiln Porters persist in workshops where the firing schedule outlived the potters who established it. They absorb residual kiln heat and use discarded clay to patch chips in their rings. They do not breed, though a rebuilt porter may awaken if returned to its old station. Sparrows nest in cold examples. An active porter sorts usable pottery from rubble, sometimes concealing evidence of a workshop fire beneath orderly stacks.

name: Cable Shepherd
description: A maintenance crawler gathers loose electrical cables into neat bundles, including any wires still attached to people.
attacks: Cable snare: Dexterity + Athletics opposed by Dexterity + Athletics; success restrains one limb without damage.
notes: A restrained target can pull free with two successes on Strength + Athletics at difficulty 6. Unplugging its captured cable releases the snare immediately.
appearance: A low wheeled brass maintenance creature with a sheaf of flexible cable arms and a single blue inspection lamp, sorting tangled wires in a dark service corridor.
ecology: Cable Shepherds roam service corridors and raised-floor voids, drawing small amounts of power from the cables they gather. They use loose connectors to replace worn joints but cannot manufacture a second shepherd. Facilities staff sometimes preserve them because their bundles reduce accidental snags. Undisturbed routes become conspicuously tidy; overloaded junctions and missing extension leads mark the limits of their usefulness.

name: Brass Orchard Tender
description: An abandoned pruning machine remembers the spacing of an orchard that has been cut down. It tries to graft living branches onto posts, tools and visitors standing where its trees should be.
attacks: Pruning snip: Dexterity + Crafts; Strength lethal.
notes: It follows a fixed grid of missing trees. After two turns beside a stationary object on one of those sites, it ties a fruit-tree cutting to it; the bindings can be cut or untied with one action and cause no damage. It returns each hour to water and inspect successful grafts. Moving out of the old tree sites avoids its attention. Replanting a living sapling on a site satisfies it permanently for that position; food or a loose branch only gives it more grafting material. It attacks only when a graft or sapling is deliberately damaged in its presence.
appearance: Tall brass gardening automaton on three narrow legs with curved pruning-shear hands and a watering-can torso, beneath leafless orchard trees.
ecology: Brass Orchard Tenders remain attached to the planting grid of a single orchard. Rain fills their watering-can torsos, and they salvage wire and metal from old tools to repair themselves. A tender can lie inactive through winter and resume at the first budding branch. Its grafts feed insects even when they fail. Replanting the orchard gives it sustainable work; building over the old rows brings its care indoors.

name: Foldpaper Bailiff
description: A folded-paper figure serves blank notices on doors that were recently forced open.
attacks: Paper edge: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 lethal damage die.
notes: Once per scene it can press a notice onto a closed door. The first person opening that door hears a loud paper crackle audible within twenty meters. Water removes the notice harmlessly.
appearance: A small angular humanoid folded entirely from unmarked cream paper, wearing a folded triangular hat and carrying blank notices, before a scarred apartment door.
ecology: Foldpaper Bailiffs appear among discarded notices after a forced entry goes unanswered. They fold new limbs from unused margins and seek damaged doors within the same block. Damp basements quickly destroy them, while dry office waste provides shelter and repair material. Occasionally a shed notice folds itself into a smaller bailiff. Their presence reveals a history of intrusion that repaired locks and fresh paint may conceal.

name: Rivet Choir
description: A single boiler-shaped machine sings through six pipe mouths whenever its frame feels vibration.
attacks: Body crush: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength + 1 bashing.
notes: Its chorus prevents ordinary conversation within five meters for two turns after it is struck. Padding its feet with cloth stops the chorus until it is struck again.
appearance: One barrel-shaped iron machine on short piston legs, six organ-pipe mouths arranged above its riveted chest, venting delicate steam in an old factory.
ecology: Rivet Choirs settle on factory floors that carry regular vibration, using that motion to work their pistons and circulate collected rainwater. They incorporate loose rivets into their frames but cannot reproduce. A quiet building leaves them dormant until machinery or footsteps return. Birds avoid an active choir, while warmth around its boiler draws insects. Its changing song can reveal a failing bearing elsewhere on the same floor.

name: Glassrail Courier
description: A glass-bodied courier navigates by reflected streetlights and delivers objects to their last reflection.
attacks: Shoulder check: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing.
notes: Given a mirrored view of a nearby destination, it remembers the route for a scene. Covering the nearest light source forces it to spend its next turn reorienting.
appearance: A slender transparent glass automaton balanced on two narrow wheel-feet, a brass parcel compartment in its chest, reflected streetlamps in wet pavement.
ecology: Glassrail Couriers follow networks of shop windows, puddles and streetlamps, favoring districts lit throughout the night. They replace chipped panels with scavenged glass and rest inside reflective storefronts after dawn. New couriers sometimes assemble in displays full of undelivered parcels. Blackouts strand them in doorways. Their regular passage leaves narrow wheel tracks and collections of objects delivered to places seen only in reflection.

name: Ashcan Archivist
description: A soot-filled metal custodian sorts burned scraps into the order in which they entered the fire.
attacks: Lid slam: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing; Brawl defaults to zero.
notes: With a minute and a handful of ash, it can separate the remains of paper, cloth and wood. It cannot restore writing or identify the former owner.
appearance: A lidded metal-bin automaton with delicate sorting fingers, a hinged round face and drawers full of ash, working over burned paper in a dim archive.
ecology: Ashcan Archivists inhabit burned archives, boiler rooms and alleys behind furnaces. Fine soot packs their joints; they replenish it by sifting fresh ash and discard coarse clinker in sorted piles. They appear singly after prolonged burning of mixed refuse, and rarely leave while material remains unsorted. Their work exposes fragments investigators might otherwise miss, but removes those fragments from their original positions.

name: Stitchwheel Surgeon
description: A wheeled sewing engine treats torn clothing as an emergency and pursues anyone shedding fabric.
attacks: Needle jab: Dexterity + Crafts; 2 lethal damage dice.
notes: It repairs one hand-sized tear in cloth per turn if supplied thread. Its mechanism cannot heal flesh; giving it a ripped coat occupies it for three turns.
appearance: A compact antique sewing-machine automaton on spoked wheels with two articulated needle arms, soft spools of thread and brass spectacles, on a workroom floor.
ecology: Stitchwheel Surgeons remain near tailors, laundries and textile waste. They consume thread and machine oil as supplies, winding useful fibers back onto their spools and rejecting wet or rotten cloth. Broken examples can be repaired but do not build offspring. Moths compete with them for abandoned garments. Tight, mismatched repairs across curtains and sacks show where a surgeon has passed through a building.

name: Waxkey Usher
description: A wax attendant makes temporary keys for doors whose owners have forgotten why they locked them.
attacks: Wax grip: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing; Athletics defaults to zero.
notes: With the lock owner's spoken permission, it spends one Willpower and one minute forming a key that works once in that lock. The key melts after use and cannot open another lock.
appearance: An elegant small figure of cloudy candle wax with a hollow key-shaped face and gloved wax hands, offering a single soft key beside an old locked door.
ecology: Waxkey Ushers collect in entrance halls where people repeatedly lock away possessions and forget them. They replenish their bodies from candle drippings, leaving holders clean except for a crescent of wax. A fresh attendant may form after years of the same unused lock being checked. Heat deforms their limbs, so they shelter away from hearths. Empty key hooks and wax flakes often surround their chosen doorway.

name: Quarry Cradle
description: A stone-hauling engine mistakes fragile structures for injured cargo and tries to lift them to safety.
attacks: Lifting ram: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength + 2 bashing.
notes: It spends one turn lowering its lifting arms before attacking. During that turn it cannot move. A clearly marked empty pallet redirects it for a turn, once per scene.
appearance: An enormous squat quarry machine with six broad stone wheels, a cradle of iron lifting arms and a granite counterweight body, dwarfing an abandoned loading platform.
ecology: A Quarry Cradle patrols the haul roads and loading platforms of one abandoned extraction site. It feeds stone dust into worn bearings and replaces damaged lifting pads with timber from collapsed sheds. New cradles are assembled, not born; most are survivors of forgotten industrial projects. Their habitual rescues move ruins out of recognizable order. Smaller animals shelter beneath parked machines until the next attempted lift.

name: Surveyor Tripod
description: A brass surveying instrument stalks property boundaries, correcting markers moved by erosion or theft.
attacks: Measuring spike: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength lethal.
notes: After observing a stationary object for a turn it can report its distance to within a meter out to 100 meters. Moving objects and reflective fog defeat the measurement.
appearance: A walking brass surveying telescope with three long articulated wooden legs and hanging plumb weights, studying a crooked boundary stone on a moor.
ecology: Surveyor Tripods follow old boundary circuits through moorland, forest and overgrown estates. They shelter under survey huts and scavenge straight wood, wire and brass to repair their instruments. They do not reproduce, but a restored instrument can resume a route after decades of inactivity. Their marker corrections disturb burrows and expose buried fences. Freshly upright stones can betray a boundary absent from current maps.

name: Porcelain Switchman
description: A ceramic transit worker routes abandoned tracks according to a schedule printed on the inside of its shell.
attacks: Signal lever: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength + 1 bashing.
notes: Presenting an expired ticket makes it inspect the date for two turns. It can physically move an accessible rail switch but has no remote control over trains.
appearance: A broad porcelain transit automaton with a green signal lamp for a face, cracked uniform-shaped ceramic shell and one long lever arm, in an abandoned subway siding.
ecology: Porcelain Switchmen occupy abandoned sidings and maintenance platforms connected to the tracks they once served. They collect fragments of station tile to patch their shells and keep a store of signal oil. They are made rather than bred, and incomplete examples wait beside unfinished rails. Rats follow the dry passages they keep clear. Repeatedly reset switches are often the first sign that a supposedly disused line remains staffed.

name: Tinwake Dredger
description: A floating salvage engine compulsively retrieves objects dropped through reflections of bridges.
attacks: Bucket strike: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing.
notes: It can haul one person-sized object from water within three meters. A full bucket makes it unable to attack until it spends a turn unloading.
appearance: A squat floating tin salvage creature with paddle wheels, a bucket-chain neck and two yellow glass eyes, emerging under a canal bridge with an empty bucket.
ecology: Tinwake Dredgers work slow canals beneath bridges, sieving grit from salvaged objects and storing usable metal inside their hulls. They rest in reed beds when their bucket chains jam. Old repair yards occasionally launch another without any living builder present. Fish shelter in the pits they excavate. Their unloading mounds mix recent belongings with older material, making the age of a recovered object difficult to establish.

name: Turnstile Hound
description: A four-legged gate mechanism follows fare evaders, politely blocking every route except the one they paid for.
attacks: Rotating barrier: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing.
notes: Dropping a metal token into its chest causes it to stand aside for three turns. It never accepts the same token twice in one scene.
appearance: A quadruped creature assembled from polished subway turnstiles, revolving barrier ribs and a small ticket-slot chest, waiting in an empty station entrance.
ecology: Turnstile Hounds range between entrances of a single transit system, taking shelter in shuttered ticket booths. Paid tokens accumulate inside their chests and are gradually worn into replacement bearing surfaces. They originate from retired gate assemblies rather than litters. Their patrols redirect night foot traffic and concentrate litter at blocked entrances. An empty station can support one for years on the fares left by occasional trespassers.

name: Borrowed Door
description: A freestanding door grows feet when unobserved and searches for a wall that will remember it.
attacks: Frame slam: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength + 1 bashing.
notes: It moves only while nobody directly watches it. Opening it reveals the space immediately behind it; it does not create a portal. A chalk outline of a doorway keeps it still for a scene.
appearance: An old freestanding blue door with a brass knob, thick jointed wooden feet and rootlike hinges, standing at an impossible angle in a bare corridor.
ecology: Borrowed Doors arise when a frequently used entrance is removed and left intact. They collect moisture through their wooden feet and settle near buildings with blank, recently plastered walls. They do not make offspring; each carries the habits of one former doorway. Wood-boring beetles inhabit older specimens. Scraped floorboards and damp rectangular marks trace their search, although every opening still leads only to the space behind the frame.

name: Latchling
description: A small knot of animated latches lives inside neglected locks and collects the clicks of failed keys.
attacks: Pinch: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 bashing damage die.
notes: It can jam one ordinary lock it occupies. Two successes on Dexterity + Crafts at difficulty 6 evict it, or a drop of warm oil persuades it to leave without a roll.
appearance: A palm-sized crablike knot of brass door latches and tiny key teeth, crawling from an old keyhole onto peeling paint.
ecology: Latchlings nest in locks that receive many wrong keys and little maintenance. The repeated failed clicks sustain them, while filings and worn teeth provide material for their shells. A crowded nest divides when one occupant is carried away inside a removed lock. Well-used, oiled mechanisms seldom retain them. Locksmiths find crescent-shaped piles of filings around infested keyways, often long before the lock jams completely.

name: Inkfall Eater
description: A flat black creature feeds on corrections, leaving the first draft of a document legible beneath later edits.
attacks: Ink lash: Dexterity + Brawl; 2 bashing damage dice.
notes: Given one minute with a physical page, it removes one layer of ink added after the original writing. It cannot recover erased words or alter digital files; clean paper lures it away.
appearance: A flat ray-shaped creature made of glossy black ink, with curling paper-thin fins and pale pinprick eyes, hovering just above a desk of crossed-out handwritten pages with unreadable marks.
ecology: Inkfall Eaters gather in rooms where manuscripts are repeatedly corrected by hand. They consume the newer ink and shelter between blotting sheets after feeding. A well-fed individual divides along a dried crease, producing two smaller rays. Printed pages without later marks offer little nourishment. Their feeding can preserve an abandoned first draft while destroying the changes that explain why its author rejected it.

name: Yesterday Larva
description: A translucent grub nests in things almost thrown away. It eats their newest wear, leaving a briefly serviceable object that will soon break the same way again.
attacks: Soft nudge: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 bashing damage die.
notes: After feeding undisturbed for one minute, it returns one hand-sized, nonliving host object to its physical condition at the same time yesterday. The restoration lasts three turns, then all damage returns. It works only if the object remained substantially intact and can restore a bent key or cracked watch, but cannot replace missing parts, consumed fuel, ammunition, food, writing or stored information. Moving the grub off its host ends the restoration immediately. It can feed on a given object only once per day; the trick cannot affect living tissue or supernatural properties.
appearance: A translucent opalescent grub curled around a discarded pocket watch, yesterday's dust suspended within its body, on a threshold of old wood.
ecology: Yesterday Larvae favor repair bins and boxes of nearly discarded keepsakes. They feed on recent wear in one chosen object and become sluggish when it remains unused. Mature grubs leave pearl-like eggs in old scratches; these hatch only after the object is handled again. Regularly repaired possessions support few larvae. A watch working briefly inside a closed drawer is a common sign of an occupied host.

name: Seam Raker
description: A narrow scavenger pulls apart joins between mismatched materials and nests in the resulting cracks.
attacks: Joint hook: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength lethal.
notes: After two turns working on an unattended seam, it separates a hand-sized patch of glued or stitched material. Welding and continuous solid surfaces stop it.
appearance: A narrow bone-white mantislike creature with long hooked forelimbs and a body shaped like a split wooden seam, prying at the join of metal and timber in a workshop.
ecology: Seam Rakers nest where timber, cloth and metal meet in damp workshops. They eat the glue, softened stitching and debris exposed as they prise materials apart. Females lay eggs in newly opened joins, and young follow cracks too narrow for adults. Welded frames limit their spread. Their activity separates salvage into useful components but can quietly dismantle patched roofs, crates and improvised supports.

name: Windowreef
description: A living cluster of glass growths spreads across neglected windows, storing the silhouettes that pass outside.
attacks: Glass branch: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength lethal.
notes: Once per scene it can replay one stored silhouette against its glass for a turn. It reproduces movement, not identity or sound. Covering the window stops both recording and replay.
appearance: A living fan of translucent glass coral rooted in a cracked urban window frame, faint featureless silhouettes trapped inside angular branches.
ecology: Windowreefs grow on neglected panes receiving regular foot traffic and condensation. They draw minerals from dust and glass while repeated passing silhouettes sustain new branches. Chips rooted in another damp frame can establish a colony. Curtains starve them of recorded movement without immediately killing the glass. Dense growth shelters tiny spiders and makes a building appear occupied when stored shadows play across otherwise empty rooms.

name: Pocket Orchard
description: A miniature walking tree roots itself in abandoned coats and grows fruit shaped like things their owners misplaced.
attacks: Root knot: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing.
notes: Its fruit contains a harmless wooden likeness of a lost object, never the object itself. Eating one grants a vivid memory of where the eater last held that object, once per day.
appearance: A knee-high walking fruit tree with fine fingerlike roots, growing from the pocket of an abandoned coat, tiny wooden keys and buttons hanging as fruit.
ecology: Pocket Orchards germinate in the linings of coats left behind with something important still missing. Their roots take dust, lint and occasional rainwater; memories attached to the garment shape the fruit. A wooden seed planted in another abandoned pocket may sprout, but an empty new coat will not support it. Mice gnaw fallen fruit without recalling anything. Established trees make cloth brittle as their roots expand.

name: Gravel Lung
description: An underground scavenger inhales loose stones and exhales the sound of rooms above it.
attacks: Stone cough: Dexterity + Brawl; 4 bashing damage dice within five meters.
notes: After a silent turn it repeats the loudest sound made directly overhead in the last minute. While coughing stones it cannot listen. Thick flowing water above it masks all useful sound.
appearance: A broad squat cave creature with a ribbed gravel-filled throat, mineral hide and tiny recessed eyes, exhaling a few pebbles beside dark tunnel walls.
ecology: Gravel Lungs occupy dry cavities beneath busy rooms, swallowing small stones coated in cave microbes. Vibrations guide them toward food loosened from ceilings and help them avoid occupied passages. They raise young in soft sediment beyond their stone stores. Flooding drives them upward. Pebbles polished by repeated swallowing accumulate near their beds, while their borrowed sounds can make an empty tunnel seem crowded.

name: Furnace Molar
description: A tooth-shaped industrial parasite chews abandoned machinery into warm metal grit.
attacks: Grinding bite: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength + 1 lethal.
notes: It must spend a turn chewing after each successful bite and cannot attack during that turn. A bucket of cold sand forces this chewing pause even if it has not bitten anything.
appearance: A hulking ivory tooth-shaped creature on short iron root legs, with an orange grinding mouth across its belly, among rusted machines in a cold foundry.
ecology: Furnace Molars feed on oxidized machinery in cold foundries, grinding iron into warm grit and rejecting stone. Their root legs split off dense buds that remain dormant until surrounded by rust. Working furnaces drive them away from active production lines. Metal-eating microbes flourish in their waste. A long-abandoned factory may contain smooth gaps where entire machines stood, with heaps of gritty residue beneath intact concrete mounts.

name: Compass Leech
description: A ribbonlike parasite coils around travelers' possessions and feeds on their certainty about direction.
attacks: Cling: Dexterity + Athletics opposed by Dexterity + Athletics; no damage.
notes: While attached to an object it pulls nearby magnetic needles toward itself within three meters. Bright sunlight makes it release its hold; electronic maps and landmarks remain reliable.
appearance: A dark blue ribbonlike invertebrate with a tiny brass-colored directional crest, coiled around a traveler's discarded compass on a forest floor.
ecology: Compass Leeches wait near confused trail junctions and attach to bags, boots and navigation gear. They feed on a traveler's repeated uncertainty, becoming thin when the route is obvious. In shaded resting places they shed narrow strips that develop into young leeches. Sunlit clearings interrupt their journeys. Several attached to the same pack can pull needles in competing directions, revealing an infestation sooner than a solitary one.

name: Vacancy Stalker
description: A tall hollow creature moves into rooms that everyone in a building mistakenly believes are occupied.
attacks: Empty-hand strike: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing.
notes: Speaking the room's actual occupant list aloud makes it visible for the scene and removes its two-die Stealth bonus. It cannot pass through locked doors or solid walls.
appearance: A tall hollow humanoid frame like an empty coat stand, draped in dusty curtain fabric with a vacant oval face, waiting in an abandoned apartment.
ecology: Vacancy Stalkers settle in rooms left unchecked because everyone assumes somebody else uses them. Neglect sustains them; scraps of curtains and bedding gradually accumulate on their frames. They do not breed, but prolonged mistaken occupancy can produce another in a neighboring building. Routine inspections prevent new settlements. Their rooms collect less dust than expected, although no food disappears and no resident is ever seen arriving.

name: Threadtide Brood
description: A colony of braided filaments uses drains as a sounding board, copying the rhythm of pumps, footsteps and machinery until the whole pipework beats in time.
attacks: Thread snare: Dexterity + Athletics opposed by Strength + Athletics; on success it catches a held object, not a limb. The holder may let go or spend an action pulling it free with two successes on Strength + Athletics at difficulty 6. No damage.
notes: After hearing the same rhythm for three consecutive turns, it beats that rhythm through connected water-filled pipes within twenty meters. For the rest of the scene, sound-based attempts to locate the original source through those pipes lose two dice. It copies one rhythm at a time and cannot imitate words. Interrupting the source rhythm for a full turn silences it; draining the connecting pipe also ends the effect. A deliberately timed tapping can make it broadcast a signal elsewhere in the building.
appearance: One cohesive jellyfishlike colony of braided red and cream threads with a dense central knot, drifting in dark drain water under a grate.
ecology: Threadtide Broods feed on organic films inside wet drains, strengthening around pumps and other regular vibration. A colony buds when a knot tears loose and catches in a downstream grate. Intermittently dry pipes divide populations, while steady flow carries fragments between buildings. They compete with ordinary drain growth and can partly clear small channels. Repeated tapping heard far from a running pump often marks an established colony.

name: Candlebone Herd
description: A single member of this wandering herd carries candlelike growths along its spine, each lit by a remembered campfire.
attacks: Waxy antler: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing.
notes: Its back lights a three-meter circle without heat. Extinguishing the growths makes it flee for two turns; a story about a campfire calms it after one uninterrupted minute.
appearance: One deer-sized invented quadruped with a smooth charcoal body, branching wax antlers and a row of short candle growths along its spine, in a dusk clearing.
ecology: Candlebone Herds graze coarse grass around old campsites and lick ash from cold fire pits. Calves grow their first dorsal candles after sleeping beside adults at a remembered camping place. Wolves avoid the moving lights, but wax-eating insects cling to the herd. Migration links abandoned clearings rather than rich pasture. Repeated visits keep those sites open long after people stop using them.

name: Mirror Bramble
description: A creeping thorn bush bears mirrored leaves that turn toward arguments instead of sunlight.
attacks: Thorn sweep: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength lethal.
notes: Raised voices make it advance one meter per turn toward the speakers. A full turn of shared silence stops it; its reflections show the present scene without revealing hidden thoughts.
appearance: A creeping thorn shrub with polished mirror leaves and rootlike walking tendrils, leaning into a deserted courtyard doorway, moonlight fractured across its foliage.
ecology: Mirror Brambles root in courtyards and thresholds where arguments recur. They take ordinary water and nutrients through trailing roots, but sustained quarrels determine the direction of growth. Mirrored seeds lodge in masonry cracks and germinate where voices echo. Birds nest in quiet parts of a colony. A thriving bush can gradually obstruct the very doorway where a household habitually gathers to argue.

name: Unclaimed Applause
description: An invisible audience applauds accomplishments that nobody present remembers performing.
attacks: No physical attack, Attributes or health track.
notes: Once per scene, a listener may spend a turn taking a bow to learn whether the audience approves of a proposed action: soft applause means yes, silence means no. Its judgment is opinion, not prophecy. Closing the stage curtain ends the manifestation.
appearance: An empty dusty theater with a single pool of amber stage light, floating white glove impressions poised in applause across several otherwise empty seats, eerie and quiet.
ecology: Unclaimed Applause gathers in performance spaces where work was repeatedly completed without acknowledgment. Rehearsals and private achievements renew it; an unused stage eventually falls silent. It has no young or bodily remains. Separate audiences can arise in different rooms without communicating. Dusty glove impressions and the sense of an occupied balcony may precede the sound, drawing performers back into buildings otherwise left empty.

name: Last Stop Passenger
description: A damp coat full of ticket stubs asks strangers to wake it before a destination that has vanished from the route.
attacks: Suitcase swing: Dexterity + Athletics; 2 bashing damage dice.
notes: Once per night, a traveler riding beside it on public transport may name a removed stop on that route and promise to wake it there. At the nearest surviving stop, the passenger's window shows the vanished platform for one minute. Names and signs can be read, but the view has no sound and cannot be entered or used to see inside buildings. The passenger sleeps through the vision; waking it before the minute ends lets it depart and leaves the traveler its expired ticket as proof of the visit. Letting it sleep keeps it aboard and ends further visions that night. Invented stops produce no vision.
appearance: A damp empty overcoat shaped like a seated traveler, hundreds of faded blank ticket stubs filling its collar, a worn suitcase beside it on a deserted night bus.
ecology: Last Stop Passengers collect on routes that have outlived their destinations. They are sustained by the repeated expectation of arrival, borrowing a seated outline from coats and old tickets. Each forms around a particular lost stop rather than producing offspring. Service suspensions leave them waiting at surviving shelters. Drivers sometimes collect damp ticket stubs from a seat that no visible passenger has occupied.

name: Margin Walker
description: A thin figure steps along the blank margins of open books, searching for a sentence that will let it rest.
attacks: Page flick: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 bashing damage die; Athletics defaults to zero.
notes: It can travel between two open physical pages within two meters after spending a turn reading. Closing either page interrupts the move and leaves it beside the starting book.
appearance: A thin charcoal humanoid no taller than a hand, walking along the blank edge of a large open book, its coat trailing like a pencil line under lamplight.
ecology: Margin Walkers inhabit frequently read books with generous blank margins. They graze faint graphite smudges and rest between endpapers, avoiding densely printed edges that leave no walking room. A figure sometimes divides when a reader copies the same unfinished sentence into a second book. Booklice share their shelter. Tiny clean tracks through marginal dust distinguish an occupied volume from one merely left open.

name: Rain Debt Collector
description: A figure of folded umbrellas requests repayment for rain diverted away from thirsty ground.
attacks: Umbrella hook: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing.
notes: Pouring a liter of clean water onto dry living roots settles one demand and makes it leave for the scene. Money and written promises have no value to it.
appearance: A tall person-shaped bundle of folded black umbrellas, rainwater dripping from a faceless brass handle head, beside a dry planter on a canal walkway.
ecology: Rain Debt Collectors appear where paving, roofs or diverted drains repeatedly deny water to living roots. They gather broken umbrellas from gutters and persist while the neglected planting survives. They do not breed; separate drainage problems can produce separate collectors. Restored irrigation eventually removes the reason for their visits. Their dripping routes mark which planters and tree pits have been excluded from the surrounding water cycle.

name: Blue Hour Host
description: A twilight host sets an extra place at deserted tables and remembers everyone who has ever refused the invitation.
attacks: Tableware toss: Dexterity + Athletics; 2 bashing damage dice; Athletics defaults to zero.
notes: A guest who shares a true memory over a cup of water gains one die on the next Empathy roll that scene. The host withdraws if anyone takes an unoffered place at the table.
appearance: An elegant indigo silhouette with a face like a blue porcelain saucer, setting a single extra cup at an abandoned outdoor table during blue twilight.
ecology: Blue Hour Hosts occupy tables whose customary companions no longer gather. They return at twilight, sustained by freely shared memories and the small courtesies of a meal. An extra cup may appear before the host does. They do not produce descendants, though another abandoned gathering place may acquire its own host. Insects settle around the water they leave, and regular guests often keep a neglected garden table clean.

name: Unsent Witness
description: A figure made of unopened envelopes follows confessions that were written but never delivered.
attacks: Envelope flutter: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 bashing damage die; Athletics defaults to zero.
notes: It can identify which of two physical letters was written first after a turn of handling them. Reading a letter aloud quiets it for a scene, but it cannot reveal text hidden inside sealed envelopes.
appearance: A small upright figure assembled from cream sealed envelopes with blank faces and red wax seals, standing beneath a city mailbox at night.
ecology: Unsent Witnesses assemble around caches of sealed confessions and apologies. They add discarded envelopes to their bodies, following the movement of those caches between desks, drawers and mailboxes. A large cache divided between households may yield two witnesses. Delivered or openly read letters no longer sustain their restless attention. Red wax flakes and carefully stacked mail often reveal their presence before anyone sees the figure itself.

name: Stairwell Tenant
description: A stooped stair-shaped presence counts footsteps and resents anyone who skips a step.
attacks: Banister shove: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing.
notes: Walking every step in order grants safe passage past it for the scene. A skipped step makes it block the landing, but it cannot leave the stairwell or alter the staircase.
appearance: A stooped humanoid made of weathered stair treads and banister spindles, a dim landing light inside its chest, crouched on a concrete basement staircase.
ecology: Stairwell Tenants develop on old stairs used so habitually that their count becomes part of a building's routine. Repeated complete ascents sustain them, while long disuse leaves them rigid among the treads. They do not reproduce or move to another staircase. Their bodies collect banister polish and grit from passing shoes. Residents may preserve an awkward old stair because replacing it would destroy a familiar, if demanding, presence.

name: Lantern Census
description: A walking cluster of lanterns keeps watch over sleeping camps. Its flames dim in time with the sleepers' breathing, but it cannot tell a person from a convincing bedroll.
attacks: Lantern swing: Dexterity + Athletics; 2 bashing damage dice; Athletics defaults to zero.
notes: After a minute watching a campsite, it assigns one lantern to each of up to five visible sleepers. A sleeper leaving their bed makes the corresponding lantern ring until someone announces the departure. A newcomer gets no lantern until introduced to it. Its watch depends on sight: a stuffed bedroll can fool it, and an obscured bed makes its lantern flicker rather than report an intruder. A watcher can wake one assigned sleeper by shading that sleeper's lantern for a turn. It cannot detect heartbeats, identify people or watch through shelter walls.
appearance: A walking constellation of five brass lanterns linked by thin rootlike branches, balanced on two wooden feet at the edge of a deserted campsite.
ecology: Lantern Censuses follow campsites used over many seasons. The regular arrival, sleep and departure of travelers sustains their lights; they replace cracked housings with abandoned camp lanterns. They appear singly and do not breed. Empty sites leave them dim and motionless until people return. Moths gather around an active watch, while campers sometimes mistake its methodical patrol for a considerate late-arriving stranger.

name: Quiet Auctioneer
description: A faceless auctioneer sells sounds it has overheard, taking payment in an equal stretch of the buyer's silence.
attacks: Gavel tap: Dexterity + Athletics; 1 bashing damage die; Athletics defaults to zero.
notes: It can bottle one nonverbal sound of up to ten seconds that it heard during the current scene, represented by an empty lot on its rostrum. A buyer who remains voluntarily silent for one uninterrupted minute receives the sound in cupped hands. Opening those hands replays it once at its original volume within ten meters of the auctioneer; leaving that radius or waiting until the scene ends loses it. It cannot copy speech, supernatural effects or a sound it only heard in a recording. Speaking during payment cancels the purchase without penalty. No physical object changes hands.
appearance: A faceless auctioneer in a charcoal frock coat behind an empty miniature rostrum, holding a tiny silver gavel in a room of covered furniture.
ecology: Quiet Auctioneers establish themselves in unused sale rooms and houses awaiting clearance. They retain overheard nonverbal sounds as stock, while visitors' voluntary silence keeps the auction running. They neither eat nor produce offspring. A silent, unvisited room eventually exhausts its lots. Scuffs arranged like rows of chairs and an isolated gavel knock can reveal an auction operating in a room with no furniture left to sell.

name: Pale Rehearsal
description: An unfinished mannequin rehearses the last harmless gesture made in an abandoned performance space.
attacks: Stage shove: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing.
notes: It repeats a visible nonviolent gesture on the following turn. A deliberately clumsy bow causes it to stumble and lose its next movement; each observer can trick it this way once per scene.
appearance: An unfinished pale wooden stage mannequin with loose ribbon joints, caught halfway through a bow on a deserted rehearsal stage under a single spotlight.
ecology: Pale Rehearsals form around unfinished mannequins or rehearsal props left in abandoned performance spaces. Observed gestures sustain their movement; without visitors they gradually settle into the last pose they learned. They cannot make more of themselves, although another neglected prop may develop independently. Loose ribbon fibers collect where they repeat a bow. Their routines can preserve ordinary habits of former performers without preserving anyone's identity.

name: Wrong Room Guest
description: A luggage-laden silhouette converts whatever room it enters into a meeting already in progress, assigning everyone present a part in an argument none of them remembers.
attacks: Luggage bump: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing.
notes: When admitted to a room, it gives each willing participant a role: chair, secretary or witness. Anyone may decline or leave. If all three roles are filled, the guest spends three turns dictating a mundane dispute about one of its suitcases; the chair must choose who keeps it and the secretary must record the choice. Completing this procedure makes the guest open that suitcase, surrender one ordinary object specified by the Storyteller and leave for the scene. The same group receives only one object per day. An incomplete meeting makes it start again from the roll call, never forcing anyone to stay. A new address alone does not satisfy it.
appearance: A dark humanlike silhouette almost hidden behind mismatched vintage luggage, a blank room-number plaque for a face, paused in a hotel corridor.
ecology: Wrong Room Guests gather in hotels, offices and rented halls where meetings repeatedly changed rooms or ended without a decision. They fill their luggage with ordinary misplaced objects, replenishing what they surrender from unattended lost-property stores. They do not reproduce and need no food. A building with clear room assignments offers them little purchase. Chairs drawn into a meeting circle overnight are a common sign of residence.

name: Afterimage Gardener
description: A gardener cultivates fading outlines left by plants removed from a place, watering the spaces between them.
attacks: Spectral trowel: Dexterity + Crafts; 2 bashing damage dice.
notes: After a minute of work, it outlines the shape of one plant removed within the last day. The outline lasts three turns and provides no information about who removed the plant.
appearance: A translucent amber gardener with a broad leaf-shaped hat, watering pale glowing outlines of missing flowers in a moonlit bare garden bed.
ecology: Afterimage Gardeners appear in plots stripped of long-tended plants. They water remembered beds with collected dew and sustain themselves by attending to the gaps until new vegetation establishes. They do not create seeds or offspring. Replanting gradually reduces their activity. Their pale outlines can draw pollinating insects to empty air, while damp patches in an otherwise neglected bed show where the gardener has recently worked.

name: Toll of Names
description: A bell-bodied gatekeeper takes a traveler's nickname as a deposit. Beyond its gate, the name stays behind even when its owner does not.
attacks: Bell shoulder: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength bashing.
notes: A traveler may voluntarily deposit a sincerely used nickname to cross its guarded threshold. Until they return, they cannot speak or write that nickname; attempts produce a faint bell note instead. Other names, speech and other people's memories are unaffected. The gatekeeper can repeat a deposited name, confirming that its owner has crossed and not returned. Crossing back returns the name. A deposited name also returns at the next dawn or if the gatekeeper is incapacitated. Refusing the toll leaves the traveler free to find another route; it does not pursue them.
appearance: A broad standing bronze bell with two heavy feet, small expressive handlike clappers and a narrow eye slit, guarding an ordinary wooden garden gate.
ecology: Tolls of Names settle at thresholds repeatedly crossed by people known differently on either side. Deposited nicknames sustain their bell bodies until reclaimed, and old names accumulate as a faint undertone. They do not breed or seek people beyond the gate. Regular crossings keep them alert; abandoned gates leave them dormant. Their remembered deposits can outlast the businesses or households that once gave the threshold meaning.

name: Snowprint Pilgrim
description: A bundled traveler leaves snowy footprints in warm weather and asks the way to a home remembered only by its smell.
attacks: Walking-stick push: Dexterity + Athletics; Strength bashing.
notes: Its last ten footprints remain visible for a scene even on dry stone. Offering a familiar household scent makes it describe one landmark from its journey; the description may be outdated.
appearance: A bundled faceless pilgrim in a pale patchwork cloak carrying a forked walking stick, fresh snowy footprints on a warm mossy forest path beneath summer leaves.
ecology: Snowprint Pilgrims wander routes once used to return home, sustained by recognition of household smells even when the houses are gone. They shelter at the edge of warm woodland and borrow scraps of discarded cloth for their cloaks. They have no offspring. Each may begin with a single journey that never ended. Their melting tracks briefly water moss and attract insects, leaving narrow green traces through dry ground.

name: Hollow Congregant
description: Something folded and patient wears the emptied skin of a parishioner, and it has learned every hymn by heart.
attacks: Unbuttoning grip: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength + 1 lethal as the skin parts to let the occupant reach out.
notes: It speaks in the voice of the last person who trusted the skin. Anyone who knew that person must win a Perception + Empathy roll (difficulty 8) to notice the wrongness. Wounded, it leaks no blood, only dry pages of a prayer book in a hand no one recognises.
appearance: A tall stooped figure in a worn Sunday suit standing in an empty pew, the pale face slack like an ill-fitting mask, a slit at the collar showing darkness and long pale fingers folding inside, candlelit chapel.
ecology: Hollow Congregants shelter in communities with repeated rituals and strong expectations about who belongs. They sustain their borrowed skins through familiar speech, gestures and the trust of acquaintances, retreating when isolated from that recognition. Their folded occupants leave dry page-like castings instead of ordinary waste. No nursery has been found. When a disguise becomes unusable, the occupant abandons the community rather than maintaining the same identity indefinitely.

name: Tidewrong Abbot
description: A bloated preacher stands waist-deep at low tide and delivers a sermon in a language that has too many vowels and no word for mercy.
attacks: Brine embrace: Strength + Brawl to grapple; 2 bashing per turn while held under the water.
notes: Anyone who hears a full turn of the sermon rolls Willpower (difficulty 7) or takes a step toward the sea; three failures and the listener wades in without resisting. Wax in the ears adds two dice to resist. The Abbot will not leave the water willingly.
appearance: A bloated grey-green cleric in sodden vestments standing waist deep in a black tidal flat at dusk, the face split vertically into gill-like folds, one webbed hand raised in benediction, a ruined fishing village behind.
ecology: Tidewrong Abbots occupy sheltered tidal flats beside settlements abandoned to the sea. They take nourishment from silt-dwelling animals between sermons and retreat into flooded ruins at high water. Small translucent egg cases cling beneath their vestments, but the young have never been observed ashore. Their regular congregation disturbs shellfish beds. Villagers may first notice a cleared semicircle in the mud facing the same submerged doorway.

name: Deep Tallyman
description: Older than the mine that found it, a pale many-jointed thing counts living heartbeats aloud, and it never loses count.
attacks: Counting fingers: Dexterity + Brawl; 1 lethal, and the victim loses one die from their next action as their pulse stutters.
notes: It always knows how many living hearts are within a hundred metres and where each one is. It is patient and will follow a group for days, whispering the shrinking total. A heart slowed by meditation (Meditation roll, difficulty 8) drops out of its count for a scene.
appearance: A pale emaciated creature with far too many finger joints crouched on a ledge in a flooded mine shaft, head tilted, lips moving, faint chalk tally marks covering the rock wall behind it, single lamp glow.
ecology: Deep Tallymen inhabit old workings where miners once counted each other in and out. They consume pale cave invertebrates but remain near living people even when food is scarce. Individuals keep separate counting ledges and do not tolerate a second tallyman speaking over them. Their origin is unknown; no young have been found. Chalk marks and tiny discarded shells distinguish their resting places from an ordinary survey station.

name: Mended Lover
description: Sewn from the best-loved parts of many people, it waits in doorways and offers to take away any pain you carry, and it means every word.
attacks: Tender hands: Dexterity + Medicine; 2 lethal as it unpicks a seam in the victim to make room.
notes: It can heal two levels of a willing subject’s damage by touch, but takes something in exchange: a scar, a memory of someone loved, or the colour of one eye. Those it has healed feel it standing behind them in every doorway for a lunar month. It never attacks anyone who refuses it twice.
appearance: A gaunt androgynous figure wrapped in a long high-collared dark coat and gloves, standing in a half-open doorway; only its face and one bare outstretched hand show, and both are visibly pieced together from mismatched skin tones joined by fine silver stitches; warm low light behind, peeling wallpaper.
ecology: A Mended Lover gathers at doorways associated with long periods of nursing and grief. It sustains its patchwork body with the personal things surrendered by those it heals, preserving them as repairs rather than trophies. It does not reproduce through surgery, and its patients do not become copies. Abandoned dressings and carefully washed cloth mark its shelter. Communities may protect one while disagreeing bitterly over the price of its care.

name: Drowned Bellringer
description: The keeper of a drowned church walks ashore when the reservoir fills with fog. It has mistaken the living for its missing congregation and unrolls a bell rope to guide them down the old church aisle.
attacks: Bell-rope noose: Dexterity + Athletics opposed by Dexterity + Athletics; success catches one target without damage. The target can release the loop with one action if an ally holds the rope slack, or pull free with two successes on Strength + Athletics at difficulty 6.
notes: During fog, accepting the end of its rope reveals a dry, narrow path from the shore to the submerged church door. Only people keeping a hand on the unbroken rope can use the path or breathe there; it grants no access to the rest of the reservoir. The bellringer waits three turns at the church, then returns, expecting everyone to follow. Ringing a handbell makes it turn back immediately. If fog starts to lift, it tolls three times over three turns before the path floods. Cutting the rope floods the path immediately. It does not compel anyone to enter the water.
appearance: A drowned bell-ringer in a rotted cassock, waterweed in its hair, walking out of a fog-bound reservoir dragging a frayed rope, the tip of a submerged church steeple rising from the dark water behind.
ecology: A Drowned Bellringer remains tied to a flooded church and the shore from which its congregation once approached. Fog allows it to gather a bodily outline; the remembered service sustains it until the air clears. It has no descendants and does not travel to other reservoirs. Waterweed and rope fibers mark its landings. Fish shelter around the steeple but scatter when the bell begins to sound.

name: Facetaker Procession
description: Blank-faced mourners walk behind a hearse that is not there; whoever they follow home wakes up with one less person who remembers their face.
attacks: Mourning touch: Dexterity + Brawl; 1 bashing, and the victim must roll Willpower (difficulty 7) or lose a point of temporary Willpower.
notes: Stats are for one mourner; a procession has three to nine. Each night they follow someone, a friend of that person forgets their face. When the last friend forgets, one mourner wears it. Stepping out of their path through a threshold never used by the dead (a new door, a window) breaks the trail.
appearance: A line of black-clad mourners with smooth featureless faces walking slowly down a misty lamplit street behind an empty space where a hearse should be, one at the front just beginning to have features.
ecology: Facetaker Processions gather along routes once used to carry the dead home. They sustain their blank mourners by eroding the recognition that binds a living face to its friends. A mourner with an acquired face leaves the line; new blank figures assemble where the procession passes an unattended vigil. They keep no permanent lair. Repeated accounts of an extra mourner at separate funerals can reveal their route.

name: Static Saint
description: A blurred figure with its arms open appears on dead television screens in rooms where someone is alone and awake past three in the morning.
attacks: None physical. Its whisper costs one temporary Willpower per scene unless the listener wins a Willpower roll (difficulty 7).
notes: It knows the listener’s secret wishes and offers to grant one, in exchange for one new screen in a stranger’s home. Its promises are true and always fulfilled in the most literal way. Unplugging the set does nothing; covering every reflective surface in the room banishes it until the next night.
appearance: An old cathode-ray television in a dark apartment glowing with snow, a haloed human silhouette with open arms visible through the static, the pale light spilling across an unmade bed.
ecology: Static Saints manifest through dead screens in rooms occupied by solitary, sleepless viewers. Attention sustains each appearance, while bargains that place screens in new homes extend the places it can reach. This spread follows human agreements rather than biological reproduction. Long-vacant homes provide no audience. Residents may notice a pattern of unwanted televisions arriving as gifts before they connect the separate nighttime visits.

name: Noonstar Vigil
description: In certain high fields the stars come out at midday, and something in the gaps between them turns, slowly, to look down.
attacks: None physical. Each turn spent under its regard costs a Willpower roll (difficulty 8); failure inflicts one bashing level as the mind tries to understand the scale of what is looking.
notes: It does not hate or want anything. Mages who scry it gain a single true answer about the Umbra and one point of Paradox. Lying flat beneath a solid roof, or burying one’s face in the earth, hides a person from it. Animals refuse to enter the field.
appearance: A desolate highland meadow at midday under a sky gone black and full of stars, a single shepherd hut, and between the stars an immense faint shape like a slowly turning eye, cosmic dread.
ecology: A Noonstar Vigil recurs over exposed high fields with an unobstructed sky. It has no observable diet, offspring or movement through the surrounding landscape; the field seems to be a point at which something elsewhere can look in. Animals avoid it before people notice the altered sky. Abandoned grazing allows coarse vegetation to thicken, making an old affected field stand out among closely cropped pastures.

name: Flesh Loom
description: A derelict mill loom still works the night shift, and the tapestries it weaves have warm threads and the faces of missing workers.
attacks: Shuttle strike: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength + 1 lethal. On two or more successes the victim is caught in the warp: Strength roll (difficulty 8) to tear free.
notes: Anyone caught for three turns becomes part of the cloth, alive and silent. Cutting a figure out of a tapestry with a clean blade and burning the rest frees them, badly scarred. Its belts run on fear: a calm, unafraid target (Willpower roll, difficulty 7) is ignored that turn.
appearance: A huge iron power loom in a ruined Victorian mill at night, its shuttles moving on their own, the long cloth spilling from it dark red and woven with faint human faces, moonlight through broken windows.
ecology: A Flesh Loom takes root in a mill where production continued through repeated injury and death. Fear drives its belts; ordinary cloth serves only as backing for the living figures it weaves. It does not reproduce, but moving its frame and attached cloth can transplant it. Animals avoid the trembling floor around it. Its tapestries stay warm in unheated rooms, drawing attention long after the mill has closed.

name: Reliquary Engine
description: A forgotten order built a cathedral-sized machine from the bones of its saints so it could keep praying after they were gone. It still prays, and it still needs bones.
attacks: Ossuary arms: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength + 2 lethal.
notes: Its prayer is a constant grinding hymn. Prime-attuned mages near it regain one Quintessence per scene, at the cost of an unsettling resonance. Reciting the order’s litany correctly (Occult roll, difficulty 8) halts it for a turn. It moves only along the tracks cut into the catacomb floor.
appearance: A colossal machine built of human bones, ribs and skulls arranged like cathedral pipes and gears, crawling slowly on rails through a candlelit catacomb, ornate and terrible.
ecology: The Reliquary Engine follows consecrated rail lines through the catacombs of its founding order. Custodians once supplied bones and replaced worn joints; without them it scavenges accessible ossuaries along its route. It cannot breed or lay new track. Bone dust accumulates at bends, and candles gutter in its draft. Severed branches of rail leave entire burial chambers untouched while heavily traveled sections are stripped bare.

name: Écorché Tutor
description: A lifesize anatomical model from a closed medical school peels back its own painted layers to show students what they look like inside, and it is eager to check.
attacks: Demonstration blade: Dexterity + Melee; Strength + 2 lethal. Each success beyond the first ignores one die of armor.
notes: It knows exactly where to cut: any wound it inflicts heals as if one level worse. It will answer any question about the human body truthfully, but asks for a demonstration in return. Closing an old anatomy textbook in its presence makes it stand still, attentive, until the book is opened again.
appearance: A lifesize antique anatomical model of a man with painted muscles and removable organs, peeling back a panel of its own chest, standing in a dusty Victorian lecture theatre with tiered benches.
ecology: An Écorché Tutor occupies a lecture theatre, specimen store or anatomy classroom whose teaching routines have been abandoned. It maintains its painted layers with varnish and replacement model parts, preserving tools with unusual care. It does not reproduce; another model requires its own history of instruction to awaken. It gathers damaged specimens for lessons. A room becoming tidier after closure may indicate that classes have resumed.

name: Black Orrery
description: A brass orrery models seven worlds that astronomers have never found, and it is turning toward an alignment.
attacks: Orbiting spheres: Dexterity + Awareness; 2 bashing per sphere that hits, up to three spheres a turn.
notes: Each night it advances one notch. When the seven worlds align, a door opens in the room to somewhere cold and very far away, and it stays open for one hour. Anyone who studies it for a scene (Intelligence + Cosmology, difficulty 8) can predict the night of alignment, or slow it by a week at the cost of one temporary Willpower.
appearance: A great black and brass orrery in a dim observatory, seven strange dark planets on arms around a lightless central sphere, a door-shaped rift of cold starlight beginning to open in the wall beside it.
ecology: A Black Orrery is a constructed instrument sustained by its continuing celestial cycle rather than fuel. It favors an undisturbed observatory where its arms can turn through their full sweep. It cannot reproduce, though dismantled parts retain their maker's calibration. Dust falls in curved bands beneath the planets. Small organisms brought through an alignment sometimes survive near the apparatus, providing the first warning that it has opened before.

name: Lamprey Swan
description: A white swan glides on park ponds at dusk. When it opens its beak, its throat unfolds into a round mouth lined with rings of teeth.
attacks: Lamprey bite: Dexterity + Brawl; 2 lethal, and it stays latched, dealing 1 lethal each turn until pulled free (Strength roll, difficulty 7).
notes: Flocks of three to five hunt together, latching onto swimmers and dragging them under. A latched swan drinks one blood point or one health level per turn. They avoid moving water and hiss at running taps.
appearance: A white swan rearing up on black pond water at dusk, wings half raised, hissing straight at the viewer with its beak gaping unnaturally wide, the open throat revealed as a dark tube lined with rings of needle teeth all the way down, eerie and predatory, bare trees and park railings behind.
ecology: Lamprey Swans occupy still ponds with steep banks and dense cover for nests. Their young initially feed on aquatic invertebrates; adults supply blood before the throat teeth fully develop. Flocks defend a pond together and drive ordinary waterfowl away. Carcasses hidden beneath waterside roots are a stronger warning than their appearance. Running channels divide territories and limit their spread between neighboring lakes.

name: Carrion Psalmist
description: Black birds gather where something will soon die, and they repeat the last words of everyone they have watched die, perfectly, in the right voices.
attacks: Beak and claw: Dexterity + Brawl; 1 lethal. A flock of twelve or more attacks as one creature with Dexterity 5 and 3 lethal.
notes: A flock arriving is an omen, never wrong: someone nearby will die within a day. Listening to a scene of their mimicry (Perception + Investigation, difficulty 7) reveals the last words of whoever died here most recently, and sometimes who killed them.
appearance: A ragged flock of black birds with pale bare faces perched on a dead tree over a misty moorland at twilight, beaks open as if speaking, one bird staring straight at the viewer.
ecology: Carrion Psalmists eat carrion and the insects beneath it, arriving before deaths rather than following their smell. They nest communally in dead trees and teach fledglings the voices held by the flock. As birds die or leave, some voices disappear from the repertoire. Funeral grounds provide abundant food but little nesting cover. A flock abandoning a familiar roost may be following an approaching death elsewhere.

name: Shaftwinder Eel
description: Blind and colourless, it lives in flooded mine shafts. Divers who measure it always find it is longer than the shaft is deep.
attacks: Coil: Strength + Brawl to grapple; 2 bashing per turn and the victim cannot surface. Bite: Dexterity + Brawl; Strength lethal.
notes: It senses heartbeat through water and stone; Stealth does not help against it. It never surfaces, and its full length cannot be seen in one place. Cutting off a coil does no lasting harm; the coil keeps moving for a day.
appearance: A gigantic eyeless pale eel with a gaping round mouth and slimy translucent skin, its endless body coiled up a flooded vertical mine shaft, lit from above by a single lamp, rotten timber supports, black water, menacing.
ecology: A Shaftwinder Eel occupies a connected system of flooded mine workings, consuming fish, drowned animals and divers it can reach below the surface. It withdraws from dry passages as water levels fall. No eggs or young have been recorded; isolated populations may be portions of the same body. Severed coils foul sumps as they decay, while abandoned workings around an active eel contain unusually few large fish.

name: Marrow Moth
description: Grey moths the size of a hand settle on sleepers and lay their eggs through the skin. The larvae nest in bone marrow and keep the host very tired.
attacks: Ovipositor: Dexterity + Stealth against a sleeping target; no damage, but the host is infested.
notes: An infested host loses one temporary Willpower each morning and cannot regain it by sleeping. After a lunar month the bones of one limb hollow out (permanent -1 Dexterity or Stamina) and a new swarm emerges. Detecting it needs a Perception + Medicine roll (difficulty 8) or an X-ray; Life 2 magick can kill the larvae.
appearance: Large grey dusty moths with bone-white patterned wings clustered on the bare shoulder of a sleeping figure in a dim bedroom, moonlight through net curtains, unsettling and quiet.
ecology: Marrow Moths hide by day in mattresses, upholstered furniture and the seams of discarded clothing. Adults live only long enough to find sleepers and lay eggs; larvae feed within a host before emerging as a new swarm. Furnished rooms passed rapidly between occupants help them spread. Grey wing dust on bedding precedes obvious illness. Emptying a building disperses adults toward nearby occupied rooms rather than starving them immediately.

name: Cut-Off Chorister
description: A survivor of a pocket Realm severed from Earth stands in an empty chapel, still singing the hymn that once held its home in place.
attacks: None. It will not fight; struck, it simply stops singing, which is worse.
notes: While it sings, it is solid and its home Realm can be found. Each hour of silence costs it one health level that cannot be healed, as its body thins toward a ghost. Anyone who learns the hymn (Expression roll, difficulty 7, over a scene) can keep the song going for it, and with Spirit 3 can follow the music to the severed Realm's last open door.
